shape: Each step's type-specific fields sit at the TOP LEVEL (never under a sub-object); `name` is required on every step. BUT `step_type` is a TAGGED OBJECT `{"type":"Agent"}`, NOT a bare string (serde internally-tagged); same for `output_format` (`{"type":"Structured"}`) and the workflow `trigger` (`{"type":"Manual"}`). `workflow_create_draft`/`workflow_update` also accept a bare-string `step_type` and wrap it, but the canonical form `workflow_get` returns is the tagged object.

optional: read_only_repos (array of absolute local Git repository paths; Claude Code/Codex on macOS/Linux only; grants reads including Git history and denies writes, even with full_access; no templates; missing paths or overlap with the working directory fail before launch)

agent_settings.tools ({cli:[...], kronn_internal:[...]}; omitted = today's launch with every tool, the project MCPs, the skill listing and the Kronn catalogue; declared = only these: `cli` lists Claude Code built-in tools (Read, Grep, Bash…, Claude Code only), `kronn_internal` lists Kronn tools loaded with their schemas and no other MCP server; both empty = no tool at all. Claude Code, Codex and ACP agents; the direct CLI fallback refuses it)
multi_agent_review (bool — second agent debates the output)
room_id (Claude Code/Codex only; template rendering to a discussion id — the step's agent is a member and principal of that room at every launch and resume, no kr-join token)
Agent.OUTPUT_PIPING: With output_format {type:TypedSchema,schema:{...}} (or Structured), the agent's emitted JSON is captured as `{{steps.<name>.data}}`, with nested access `{{steps.<name>.data.<field>}}` / `{{steps.<name>.data.arr.0.k}}` (`data_json.<field>` works identically). THIS is how you feed a deterministic ApiCall/Exec step from an LLM step. TYPED INJECTION in an api_body: a field whose value is EXACTLY one placeholder is replaced by the REAL typed JSON (arrays/objects preserved, not stringified) — write it QUOTED as a normal string leaf. E.g. a review step emits {verdict, generalComment, inlineComments[]} and the next ApiCall posts api_body = {"event":"{{steps.review.data.verdict}}", "body":"{{steps.review.data.generalComment}}", "comments":"{{steps.review.data.inlineComments}}"} — `comments` arrives as a real array. (A placeholder embedded in surrounding text, e.g. "PR #{{n}}", stays a string.) To run a Quick Prompt's logic in a PIPEABLE way, put its `quick_prompt_id` on an Agent step with TypedSchema — NOT BatchQuickPrompt (see its note).

PublishPageData.note: Typed, zero-token sink for Kronn Live Pages. Each write requires dataset, operation (replace|append|upsert|clear), and value_from as one typed context path such as steps.fetch.data.series (not for clear, which empties the dataset). Upsert also requires key_field; append is idempotent per workflow run by default.

CollectApiData.note: Runs independent Quick APIs and shell-free CLI commands concurrently. Every source requires a unique alias, optional required flag/variables map, and exactly one of quick_api_id, quick_exec_id or inline quick_exec. Prefer a saved quick_exec_id from qe_list. Inline quick_exec is {command,args,timeout_secs?,output_format}; command must be a bare binary in workflow exec_allowlist, shell binaries are rejected, args stay literal, and output_format is json|csv|text|lines; CSV becomes an array of objects and each stream is capped at 1 MiB. Output is {sources:{alias:<typed extracted data>},meta:{...}}. Source variables may use run-anchored time expressions such as {{time.now|shift:-24h|floor:hour|fmt:rfc3339}}; every parallel source shares the same anchor. Optional failures yield PARTIAL; required failures stop the workflow.

TransformData.note: Deterministic zero-token JSON shaping. input_from is one typed context path; each field has target, RFC 9535 JSONPath source, operation (copy|count|sum|average|min|max|first|last), optional fallback and optional value_type (string|number|boolean). JSONPath source is relative to the value resolved by input_from. count returns array length, object key count, string length, 0 for null, or 1 for another scalar. fallback is used BEFORE the operation: fallback 0 followed by count therefore yields 1; use fallback [] to count missing collections as zero, or omit fallback to fail on a missing required path.

optional: api_response ({"type":"Binary","accept":["image/*"],"max_bytes":262144} for a file: data {content_type,size,base64,data_uri}; extract $.data_uri for a Page . Cap max 2097152; an undeclared type or a larger body fails the step)
ApiCall.note: plugin_slug + config_id MUST exist in mcp_list. endpoint_path is INDICATIVE — any valid path on the API works; set api_method explicitly for a non-GET on an unlisted path.

optional: exec_stdin (piped to stdin — use for LARGE input instead of a huge arg, no argv size limit)

exec_script_files ([{path, sha256}] — repository files the command runs: the entry script and the modules it loads, relative to the home project's repository; an empty sha256 is pinned to the current content at save. The command runs from a verified copy (cwd = the copy, env KRONN_WORKTREE = the run's checkout) and fails before running, naming the file, when one changed since approval)
Exec.note: exec_command binary MUST be in the workflow `exec_allowlist`. Each exec_args entry is one literal argv string, but an interpreter's inline code (`bash -c`, `python3 -c…`, `node -e` / `--eval=…`, `perl -e`, attached or clustered forms included) is parsed as code: it accepts no template value except `{{run.id}}` and `{{time.now…}}`, not even through `|sh`. Pass the value as a later argument the interpreter never parses, e.g. `bash` + `["-c", "echo \"$1\"", "_", "{{issue.title}}"]`, or `sys.argv[1]` in Python, or `["-e", "console.log(process.argv[1])", "--", "{{issue.title}}"]` in Node (the `--` is required: Node, Perl, Ruby and PHP keep reading options after their code), or via exec_stdin. A value must never sit where the interpreter still reads options (before the inline code or a `--`): `["{{mode}}", …]` is refused. Saving refuses anything else, and a saved step that still does it is refused at run time. Code and data are separate: the inline code or script is the program, a run value is data it reads (`sys.argv`, `process.argv`, `"$1"`, or exec_stdin read with `json.load(sys.stdin)`); exec_stdin is never code (`bash` without `-c` or `python3 -` reading it is refused). An Exec line an agent writes that takes any run value (args, stdin, setup or a source) is saved but refused at run time until a human approves it in the workflow editor, even in a data-only shape; an agent cannot give, imply or bypass that approval. The save result's `kronn_readiness` lists each such line as a `human_only` blocker: tell the user which steps to approve, never call the workflow ready.

optional: gate_request_changes_target (step name to loop back to on 'request changes')
gate_checkpoint_before (commit the run worktree before the gate; isolated runs only)

BatchQuickPrompt.OUTPUT_PIPING: When batch_wait_for_completion=true, `{{steps.<name>.data.results}}` is an ordered array of `{index, discussion_id, item, output, tokens_used, tokens_status}`. `output` is the complete final Agent message from that child discussion (not truncated), so an Exec/ApiCall can consume the fan-out deterministically without an Agent collector. The data envelope also carries aggregate `tokens_used` plus `tokens_status` (`measured`, `partial`, or `unavailable_children_not_measured`). Fire-and-forget mode returns results=[] and tokens_status=pending because children are still running.

optional: api_response (as ApiCall: one file per item)
BatchApiCall.note: fan one ApiCall over a list without starting a model.
BatchApiCall.PER_ITEM_VARS: Each item's fields are templatable in api_endpoint_path AND api_body/api_query as `{{batch.item.<field>}}` (canonical), `{{item.<field>}}` (alias), and bare `{{<field>}}`. So a per-item path works: `/comments/{{batch.item.commentId}}/reactions`. Also `{{batch.index}}` (0-based) and `{{batch.item}}` (whole item as JSON). NOTE: this is a DIFFERENT name from the SubWorkflow-foreach item (`current_task.*`) — batch fan-out uses `batch.item.*`/`item.*`.

JsonData.note: deterministic data source that starts no model — feeds {{steps.<name>.data}}. Use an actual JSON value (object, array or scalar), not JSON serialized into a string. Preserve the requested payload and its object/array shape exactly; examples illustrate syntax only.

optional: sub_workflow_foreach_file (workspace-relative JSON array → child runs once per item)
sub_workflow_variables ({childVariable: template} rendered in this run; the child's snapshot is prepared like a manual launch; in foreach it may read {{current_task.*}})
SubWorkflow.FOREACH_RUNTIME_CONTRACT: RUN-BREAKING. `sub_workflow_foreach_file` is YOUR source list (any name, e.g. .kronn/prs.json). Before each child run the engine exposes the CURRENT item to the child TWO ways: (1) TEMPLATE VARS — each top-level field as `{{current_task.<field>}}` (e.g. an ApiCall path `/repos/o/r/pulls/{{current_task.number}}/reviews`, a worktree `.kronn/pr-{{current_task.number}}`); scalars stringify, null→"", nested arrays/objects render as compact JSON, and the whole item is `{{current_task}}`. The accessor name is FIXED `current_task.*` (it mirrors the file, NOT the source-file name; it is NOT `{{item.*}}` or `{{foreach.*}}`). (2) FILE — the same item is written to the FIXED path `.kronn/current_task.json` in the shared worktree, for an Agent/Exec step that needs the full object. Bookkeeping vars `{{__subwf_item_id__}}` (=item `id`) and `{{__subwf_item__}}` (index) are also set.
SubWorkflow.FOREACH_CONCURRENCY: SubWorkflow foreach is intentionally SEQUENTIAL in the parent worktree. Workflow-level `concurrency_limit` controls overlapping FULL workflow runs; it does not parallelize foreach items. A limit above 1, or a `concurrency_key` (runs with different keys overlap), is accepted only with `workspace_config.require_isolation: true`, where each run owns its worktree and its own sequential foreach; otherwise it is rejected at save. Use BatchQuickPrompt for parallel agent fan-out.

optional: sub_workflow_variables ({childVariable: template} rendered in this run)
TriggerWorkflow.note: Launches the target workflow as an INDEPENDENT run and continues at once (fire and forget), unlike SubWorkflow which waits and shares the worktree. The child is created like a manual launch: it must be enabled, its required variables must be mapped, its own concurrency_limit/concurrency_key applies, and it gets its own worktree, budget and lifecycle (cancelling the parent does not cancel it). Loops between workflows are allowed (review → rework → review); a chain of more than 20 runs launching one another is refused. Mapped names must be child launch variables; a template may not read a parent variable resolved from project_env/kronn_context (declare the secret on the child). Output data: child_run_id, child_workflow_id, child_workflow_name, variables (names only), concurrency_key; signal TRIGGERED. A refusal (disabled child, missing variable, key at its limit, …) fails the step with status/signal TRIGGER_REFUSED, branchable via on_result. The child's run carries triggered_by_run_id; the parent's step result carries child_run_id.

DelegateSubtasks.note: Runs the parent task's subtasks without an orchestrator agent: launches each ready subtask (plan order, blockers, concurrency) with the worker of its first `worker:<key>` tag found in worker_map ({key: {agent, tier?, model?}}, native workers only), else default_worker; waits on the executions' durable state with no model call; reviews each delivery in ONE fresh session of `agent` (DoD, diff, worker report) whose verdict is approve | request_changes | reassign | escalate; integrates approved work into the target branch, validations included. Output data: discussion_id, campaign_id, target_branch, review_calls, subtasks[{task, status, integrated_sha, review_rounds, attempts, integration_conflicts, worker, cost_usd, tokens}]. Signals: OK (all integrated, success) or, as a failed step routable by on_result, ESCALATED (round cap or reviewer escalation), CONFLICT (a subtask conflicted twice on integration), BLOCKED (human hold, dirty target, nothing launchable, LLM budget), FAILED, TIMEOUT. Executions are never cancelled by a stop; re-running the step resumes them. Forbidden in on_failure.

TaskBoard.note: Zero-token board over the planning tasks sharing one tag, columns todo|in_progress|done. operation: read|add (title, description, tags comma-separated)|toggle (task)|move (task, before = a task id or __col_<column>__, column)|edit (task, title, description)|discuss (task; the step's agent). Never touches a task without the tag. data.rows = open cards in board order, recent done ones, then one __col_<column>__ marker per column: publish it with PublishPageData value_from steps.<name>.data.rows.

discovery_rule: Do not infer the available step types from one workflow: step_types_closed_set is the complete taxonomy. To adapt an existing workflow, call workflow_list and then workflow_get with an id actually returned by that list; no named example is guaranteed to exist.

triggers.Cron: {"type":"Cron","schedule":"0 7 * * 1-5","timezone":"Europe/Paris"}: five-field cron; `timezone` (IANA) is optional, absent = Kronn's global timezone (Settings; default the machine's), so pass `UTC` for a UTC schedule. DST: a local time the spring change skips does not fire that day; one the autumn change repeats fires once.
triggers.Tracker: {"type":"Tracker","source":{"type":"GitHub","owner":"o","repo":"r"},"query":"","labels":[],"interval":"*/10 * * * *"}: one run per new issue (UTC interval).
triggers.Watch: {"type":"Watch","api_plugin_slug":"github","api_config_id":"<config>","api_endpoint_path":"/repos/o/r/commits","api_query":{},"interval":"*/5 * * * *","timezone":null,"detection":{"type":"Validators"}} (or `quick_api_id` instead of the api_* fields). Polls the source with a GET through the API broker (stored credentials, default headers) and creates a run ONLY when it changed; a poll creates no run. Detection: the stored ETag/Last-Modified go out as If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since (304 = unchanged); on a 200, `Validators` compares ETag/Last-Modified (body fingerprint when absent), `Body` the body fingerprint, `{"type":"JsonPath","path":"$.items[*].id"}` the fingerprint of that extract. The first poll records a baseline without a run. Interval: five fields, at most once a minute, read in `timezone` like a Cron. An unadmitted change (concurrency limit, preflight) is detected again next poll. The run reads `{{trigger.*}}`.

template_vars.syntax: `{{namespace.path}}` in any string field (prompt_template, api_endpoint_path, api_query/api_body values, exec_args/exec_stdin, gate_message, notify_config, …). Dotted nested access works incl. array index: `{{steps.plan.data.subtasks.0.title}}`. An UNKNOWN ref is left VERBATIM in previews and rejected before execution, so a typo never reaches an agent, command or external API. `{{path|sh}}` renders the value as one POSIX single-quoted shell word (a quoting helper, never accepted inside Exec inline code). The one explicit fallback is `{{path ?? "text"}}` (or `'text'`, no escapes): it renders the literal when the path is absent or JSON null, e.g. `{{steps.check.data.stdout ?? ""}}` after a Goto skipped `check`; such a ref may name a later step but never an unknown one.

namespaces.steps.<name>.data: structured payload (Structured/TypedSchema agent, ApiCall/Exec/JsonData envelope). Nested fields: `steps.<name>.data.<field>` (incl. array index). Strings unwrapped for clean interpolation. In an api_body, a field whose value is EXACTLY one such placeholder is injected as the REAL typed JSON (array/object preserved) — write it quoted, e.g. `"comments": "{{steps.review.data.inlineComments}}"`.
namespaces.steps.<name>.data_json: same payload; `data_json.<field>` resolves identically to `data.<field>` (alias). In a prompt/string it renders verbatim JSON; in an api_body whole-placeholder field it injects typed JSON just like `data`.
namespaces.steps.<name>.summary / .status: the envelope summary line / OK|… status.
namespaces.previous_step.{output,data,data_json,sum: shorthand for the immediately preceding step.
namespaces.batch.item.<field> / item.<field> / <fie: the current item inside a BatchApiCall / BatchQuickPrompt fan-out (templatable in api_endpoint_path + body/query). `{{batch.index}}` = 0-based index, `{{batch.item}}` = whole item JSON.
namespaces.current_task / current_task.<field>: the current item inside a SubWorkflow foreach child (DIFFERENT name from batch fan-out's `batch.item.*`; see SubWorkflow.FOREACH_RUNTIME_CONTRACT).
namespaces.state.<key>: run state written by a step via a `---STATE:<k>=<v>---` line; persists across Gate pauses + Goto loops. An Exec's markers are read from its raw stdout, where a value may span lines up to its closing `---`.
namespaces.artifacts.<name>: content a step emitted via a `---ARTIFACT:<name>---` block.
namespaces.run.id: id of the current workflow run (a SubWorkflow child run has its own).
namespaces.run.artifacts_dir: absolute path of a directory Kronn creates for this run, outside every checkout (each run has its own; a SubWorkflow child too). Exec steps write files there (screenshots, logs, large reports); a Claude Code or Codex Agent step whose prompt names this path reads it read-only (same policy as read_only_repos: --add-dir, Edit denied, mandatory sandbox). Removed when the run ends; kept while it waits for approval or is interrupted.
namespaces.ref:<kind>:<slug>: local id of another resource, kind one of workflow, qe, qa, prompt, skill, plugin, artifact; resolved at run start in the run's project, then the global scope (identity of a kronn/ import, else the slug of the resource's name). Unknown or ambiguous fails the step before launch. Structured id fields (sub_workflow_id, quick_prompt_id, quick_api_id, batch_quick_prompt_id, CollectApiData quick_api_id/quick_exec_id) also accept `ref:<kind>:<slug>`, stored as the local id at save. Scripts: GET /api/resources/resolve?ref=<kind>:<slug>&project=<id>.
namespaces.project.<path>: the run's project profile `kronn/project.toml` (schema v1: validation.targets.<name>.command, forge.{base_branch,merge_method,required_approvals,pr_template,labels.<name>.{name,triggers}}, tracker.{kind,project_key,statuses.<name>,transitions.<name>.{from,to}}, delivery.workflows.<name>.{workflow,inputs.<input>}). Read once at run start at the commit of the main checkout's default-branch ref (origin/HEAD's branch, else main, else master; local branch first), never from the run's worktree, and pinned with the run: resumes and child runs see the same values. A table or array renders as JSON, items by index. A read without `??` fails the run before its first step when the profile or key is missing; use it for repository-specific values instead of hard-coding them. Reserved name.
namespaces.trigger.{body,body_truncated,status,etag: Watch-trigger fields: the response that changed, credentials removed, body cut at 64 KiB (`body_truncated`); `extract` only in JsonPath mode, `etag`/`last_modified` only when the server sent them (use `?? ""`).
namespaces.time.now / now: one timestamp captured at run start and reused by all steps and parallel CollectApiData sources, including after resume. `now` is shorthand; `run.*`, `time.*`, `now*`, `project.*` are reserved names.
namespaces.<launch_var>: any `variables[].name` is referenced bare as `{{name}}`. Its source is user_input (default), project_env with source_ref `<env.NAME>`, or kronn_context with `<context.key>`. References resolve at run start; never store the resolved value.

filters.shift: +/- fixed duration; units s, m, h, d, w; 10-year safety limit
filters.tz: IANA timezone such as Europe/Paris; Kronn's global timezone (Settings) by default
filters.floor: minute | hour | day; day boundaries use the selected timezone

time_expressions.vendor_neutrality: Do not use plugin/vendor names such as fmt:adobe. Adobe's YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSS without Z is fmt:local_iso_ms; GitHub uses rfc3339; Jira day parameters use date; epoch APIs use unix or unix_ms.
time_expressions.ordering: Filter order is declarative: Kronn applies the shift to the run anchor, converts to the requested timezone, floors there, then formats.

template_vars.batch_quick_prompt_results: `steps.<name>.data.results` is the ordered, complete BatchQuickPrompt payload list after completion; use `data.results` / `data_json.results` for deterministic downstream piping.

discovery_order: qa_list/qe_list: prefer and resolve saved Quick APIs or Quick Execs; keep inline quick_exec for one-offs and add each CLI binary to exec_allowlist
page_list: reuse a matching shared Page; otherwise page_create
workflow_step_schema: compose the three typed configs
workflow_create_draft: save disabled for human review
data_pipeline_contract.direct_publish: TransformData is optional when the Page intentionally consumes the complete lossless collector envelope. Then bind value_from directly to steps.<collect-name>.data.
data_pipeline_contract.page_contract: A Page is shared and is not owned by one workflow. page_publish.page_id stores the configured link; several workflows may target the same Page.
